body.claim: A rung with more than one candidate must fall through rather than select, and must never be a tiebreak.
body.detail: Falling through matters because later rungs carry strictly more information: content identity cannot separate two textually identical functions, but the symbol path can. Terminating at the first ambiguity detached 602 of 2095 anchors on a real corpus; falling through reduced it to 121 without ever selecting among equals.

body.claim: The table is keyed by symbol and kind together, and holds node ids valid only in the tree it was built from.
body.detail: Keying on the pair is what stops a struct Foo and an impl Foo counting as two declarations of one name, so ambiguity is judged within a kind rather than across the whole file. The stored values are tree-sitter node ids, which are derived from the node address in one parse: a table built from one tree and queried with nodes from another will match nothing, or worse, match by coincidence. Build and query in the same parse.

body.claim: Project documentation is written in a plain declarative register: no slogans, no one-word paragraphs or sentence fragments for emphasis, no aphoristic closings, and headings that name a subject rather than announce a reaction.
body.detail: Raised on the README, which opened on a slogan and used repetition for rhythm; the same pass was then applied to CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md. The objection was that it read as marketing rather than as documentation for infrastructure. Applies to README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and anything a reader meets before the code. Bold lead-ins on a list of practices are fine where they state a fact rather than announce a reaction. Error messages and commit messages keep their own voice. Recorded here because lint-docs is where documentation properties are enforced, and because README.md itself cannot be anchored: no language adapter is registered for it.
